title: Station 1 — Belt Motor Overheat
content:
Root cause: Belt motor winding insulation class F degradation from sustained high temperature. Dust buildup on heatsink increases thermal resistance by 30-50%. Ambient temperature >40°C in enclosed cabinet accelerates degradation.

Symptoms: Temperature sensor readings above 50°C. Belt speed drops as motor deratesautomatically. Possible brownouts if thermal protection triggers.

Repair: (1) Clean motor vents and heatsink — expected temp reduction 8-12°C. (2) Verify ambient ventilation is adequate. (3) Reduce inspection dwell time by 15% if symptom persists. (4) Replace motor windings if insulation resistance <1 MΩ.

Prevention: Monthly thermal inspection. Install temperature logging. Check fan operation weekly.

title: Station 1 — Belt Roller Vibration Anomaly
content:
Root cause: Belt roller bearing inner race spalling (BPFO defect at 3.2x shaft speed). Dynamic imbalance of drive pulley >5g·mm. Shaft misalignment >0.05mm.

Symptoms: Vibration sensor >25 mm/s RMS. Blade chatters intermittently. Product positioning errors at station sensor.

Repair: (1) Apply grease to bearings — if vibration >35 mm/s, full replacement is needed. (2) Check belt tension and pulley alignment. (3) Balance drive pulley if runout >0.1mm.

Prevention: Vibration trending — schedule bearing replacement at 8000 hours MTBF.

title: Station 1 — Belt Slippage
content:
Root cause: Belt surface glazing (friction coefficient drops from 0.35 to 0.20). Tension spring fatigue — free length increased >10%. Drive pulley lagging rubber hardened (Shore A >80 vs spec 60).

Symptoms: Product moves slower than expected. Belt stutters visible in Factory I/O. Cycle times increase.

Repair: (1) Clean belt surface with isopropyl alcohol. (2) Adjust tensioner to restore spec tension. (3) Replace lagging rubber if hardness out of spec. (4) Replace belt if glazing is extensive.

Prevention: Belt inspection every 6000 hours. Tension check monthly.

title: Station 2 — PCB Gripper (Vacuum Cup) Failure
content:
Root cause: Vacuum cup Shore A hardness drop from 55 to 40 after 500k cycles. Cup lip permanent deformation >0.5mm. Venturi orifice wear reduces vacuum flow 25%.

Symptoms: Pick & Place drops lid during transfer. Item detected sensor does not confirm grip. Assembly failure at Station 2 output.

Repair: (1) Replace vacuum cup — 30 min downtime. (2) Clean venturi orifice. (3) Check vacuum generator flow rate. (4) Inspect cup mounting surface for flatness.

Prevention: Cup replacement every 3000 hours. Weekly vacuum level check.

title: Station 2 — Pick & Place Axis Jam
content:
Root cause: Linear guide ball screw backlash >0.1mm from wear. Guide rail lubrication interval exceeded — grease thickening. Particulate contamination in ball nut from machining chips.

Symptoms: P&P axis does not complete movement within timeout. Moving X/Z sensors remain active. Cycle time increases significantly.

Repair: (1) Lubricate guide rails and ball screw — use specified grease (ISO VG 150). (2) Check backlash with dial indicator. (3) Clean ball nut if contaminated. (4) Replace ball screw if backlash >0.2mm.

Prevention: Lubrication every 5000 hours. Clean ball nut quarterly.

title: Station 3 — Positioning Bar Jam
content:
Root cause: Cylinder rod seal extrusion (O-ring compression set). Operating pressure below 4 bar. Cylinder rod contamination causing increased friction.

Symptoms: Clamped sensor does not confirm within mechanical timeout. Bar raise/lower takes longer than normal. Cycle time increases by 30-50%.

Repair: (1) Check pneumatic pressure — minimum 5.5 bar required. (2) Clean cylinder rod. (3) Replace O-ring seals if extruded. (4) Check flow control valve settings.

Prevention: Pneumatic system inspection every 15000 hours. Replace seals proactively at 8 years.

title: Station 4 — Wiring Connection Stop Blade Fault
content:
Root cause: Station 4 is a timed stop station for simulated wiring harness installation. The main failure modes are belt slippage preventing proper product positioning at the stop blade, and sensor drift causing false product detection.

Symptoms: Product does not reach stop blade position. Wiring timer starts before product is fully stopped. Cycle time deviation.

Repair: (1) Check belt tension and surface condition. (2) Verify stop blade actuation full stroke. (3) Clean entry and station sensors.

Prevention: Weekly sensor cleaning. Belt inspection monthly.

title: Station 5 — Back Cover Pusher Jam
content:
Root cause: Pusher cylinder rod seal failure causing pneumatic leak. Operating pressure below 4 bar. Cylinder rod side-load from misaligned back cover causing binding.

Symptoms: Pusher extended sensor does not confirm. Pusher retracted sensor does not confirm. Press cycle timeout. Back cover not fully seated on product.

Repair: (1) Check pneumatic supply pressure (min 5 bar). (2) Verify pusher cylinder alignment — check for side-load. (3) Replace cylinder rod seals. (4) Check extended/retracted limit switch positions.

Prevention: Pneumatic maintenance per ISO 4414. Cylinder seal replacement every 10000 cycles.

title: Station 6 — Vision Sensor Error
content:
Root cause: Camera CCD hot pixel degradation. Lens contamination (oil mist, cutting fluid aerosol). Backlight LED driver PWM fault causing flicker. CPU thermal throttling at >85°C die temperature.

Symptoms: Vision sensor returns wrong product type code. False PASS or FAIL results. Increased reject rate or good parts going to reject bin.

Repair: (1) Clean camera lens with appropriate solvent and microfibre. (2) Verify LED backlight operation. (3) Check ambient lighting — no direct sunlight or reflections. (4) Recalibrate vision sensor with known-good reference parts. (5) Check CCD temperature with thermal camera.

Prevention: Weekly lens cleaning. Annual CCD calibration verification.

title: Station 7 — Pivot Arm Sorter Jam
content:
Root cause: Pivot bearing seizure from grease breakdown (operating temp >60°C). Pneumatic 5/2 valve spool sticking from moisture or contamination.

Symptoms: Sorter arm does not move to commanded position. Products going to wrong bin. Good rate drops significantly.

Repair: (1) Check pneumatic supply to sorter valve. (2) Cycle valve manually to check for sticking. (3) Replace valve if spool is contaminated. (4) Inspect pivot bearing — lubricate or replace. (5) Check arm physical obstructions.

Prevention: Annual valve replacement. Bearing grease every 12 months. Clean compressed air supply — install coalescing filter.

title: All Stations — Power Supply Brownout
content:
Root cause: 24VDC PSU output ripple >5% from filter capacitor ESR increase. Contactor auxiliary contact bounce >5ms. Loose wire terminal on DIN rail (torque <0.5Nm). Mains voltage fluctuation ±10% outside IEC 61000-4-11.

Symptoms: Belt turns off briefly (0.3-0.8s). Actuators de-energise momentarily. Factory I/O shows coil state changes not commanded by PLC.

Repair: (1) Check PSU output with oscilloscope — ripple must be <200mV. (2) Inspect all DIN rail terminal torques (0.5-0.8 Nm). (3) Replace PSU if capacitors are aged. (4) Install UPS for critical stations.

Prevention: PSU replacement every 7-10 years or 50000 hours. Terminal torque check annually.

title: All Stations — Diffuse Sensor Drift
content:
Root cause: LED emitter degradation (luminous flux -20% after 50k hours). Lens contamination from dust, oil mist. Background suppression reference shift from temperature changes. EMI from variable frequency drives coupling into unshielded cables.

Symptoms: False product detections. Missed product arrivals. Intermittent sensor output. Station timeout or deadlock.

Repair: (1) Clean sensor lens with dry compressed air then isopropyl wipe. (2) Verify sensing range — hold calibration target at operating distance and check output. (3) Replace sensor if LED output is degraded below threshold. (4) Check cable shielding continuity.

Prevention: Sensor cleaning monthly. Calibration check quarterly. Sensor replacement at 50000 hours or 5 years.

title: Warehouse — Stacker Crane Position Drift
content:
Root cause: Absolute encoder battery backup voltage <2.8V causing position loss on power cycle. Encoder glass disk contamination. Resolver coupling set screw loosening from vibration.

Symptoms: Crane stores to wrong cell. Retrieval misses cell position. Position register value drifts from expected.

Repair: (1) Replace encoder battery (typically CR2032). (2) Re-home crane to cell 55 (rest position) and verify register. (3) Run calibration cycle through all 54 cells. (4) Check resolver coupling torque.

Prevention: Battery replacement every 3 years. Encoder calibration at annual maintenance.

title: OEE Analysis — Production Line Performance
content:
OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) = Availability × Performance × Quality.

Target values for this TV assembly line:
- Availability: >90% (downtime <10% of schedule)
- Performance: >85% (actual rate vs ideal rate)
- Quality: >95% (pass rate at Station 6)
- Target OEE: >72.7% (world-class)

Common OEE losses:
1. Equipment Failure (Availability): Motor faults, sensor failures, jams
2. Setup & Adjustment (Availability): Changeovers, tool changes
3. Minor Stoppages (Performance): Sensor misdetects causing cycle pauses
4. Reduced Speed (Performance): Belt slip, thermal derating
5. Process Defects (Quality): Vision sensor errors, assembly failures
6. Startup Rejects (Quality): Products after restart before calibration

Improvement actions: Implement predictive maintenance on bearings and belts. Add automatic sensor cleaning cycles. Use run_line.py fault injection to test recovery procedures.
